decision_reason: A1 gives lying on right side versus lying on back only a questionable smoothness distinction, while stepper versus cross trainer differs only in intensity. Add gravity-relative lateral torso inclination and bilateral leg alternation as independent, observable concepts. Leg alternation connects running and stepper to seen walking and cycling anchors while distinguishing them from synchronous jumping or rowing motion. Preserve the other concepts rather than inventing elevator-specific signatures or assuming equipment-handle use. Standing versus standing in an elevator still, and stepper versus cross trainer, may remain ambiguous. The supplied distances guide semantic priorities and do not establish recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: lateral_torso_inclination
attributes.definition: Magnitude of the gravity component along the torso's anatomical left-right axis, reflecting sideways torso inclination rather than forward-backward inclination or rotation about gravity.

levels.Low: Gravity has little or no component along the torso's left-right axis.
levels.Medium: Gravity has a moderate component along the torso's left-right axis.
levels.High: Gravity is predominantly aligned with the torso's left-right axis.

attributes.name: leg_motion_alternation
attributes.definition: Prominence of repeated left-right alternation in bilateral leg motion, independent of repetition rate or overall motion magnitude.

levels.Low: Little or no repeated left-right alternation; legs are largely stationary or move together.
levels.Medium: Left-right alternation is intermittent or mixed with nonalternating leg motion.
levels.High: Repeated left-right alternation is a dominant and sustained leg-motion pattern.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable acceleration and angular-motion magnitude across the available body sensors. This retains a transferable distinction between quiet elevator standing and active movement, and between moderate and vigorous exercise. Effort, technique and equipment resistance can change signal magnitude, so intensity alone is not a reliable stepper versus cross trainer discriminator.

cadence: G6 supports repeated cycles in leg and torso motion, connecting running to walking and stepper to other cyclic exercise. Ambiguity arises from counting steps versus full bilateral cycles, harmonics, voluntary pace and short windows; comparisons must use a consistent meaningful repetition unit.

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes in acceleration, retaining the distinction between continuous cyclic exercise and fluctuating locomotion. Technique and transition windows create ambiguity. Side-lying is not intrinsically less smooth than supine lying, so the A1 side-lying distinction should not be treated as physically established; the added orientation concept addresses that pair instead.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief acceleration changes associated with foot contacts and landings, linking running to jumping and separating impact-rich activity from supported exercise. Equipment transients and sensor movement can also produce peaks. Elevator acceleration or braking is window-dependent and does not justify a compulsory impact distinction from standing.
target_unseen: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative mean body configuration, preserving transfer from lying on back to side-lying and from upright exercise to rowing. Multiple body positions help distinguish overall configuration from isolated limb orientation. Dynamic acceleration, seated configurations and variable forward lean can obscure a single global inclination level.

posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative body orientation, providing a rowing-versus-stepper contrast beyond intensity and connecting rowing to seen activities with changing configurations. Torso and leg evidence can distinguish global changes from arm-only motion. Rowing technique, movement amplitude and short windows introduce ambiguity.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion of instrumented body segments, retaining a shared exercise component across rowing, stepper and cycling. It captures angular prominence rather than gravity-relative configuration changes. Vigorous limb rotations can coexist with a stable torso, and amplitude varies with technique.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 provides short-window evidence of linear progression, preserving the useful locomotion-versus-stationary-exercise concept. However, inertial proxies cannot establish sustained constant velocity or absolute displacement reliably. Elevator travel and treadmill versus overground distinctions are therefore especially ambiguous; retention does not validate the corresponding A1 assignments.
target_unseen: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and predictability, connecting cyclic unseen exercise to seen cyclic activities while contrasting it with unscripted movement. Quiet standing can also be highly predictable. Short windows, pauses and elevator transitions can alter apparent regularity, so elevator context alone does not warrant reduced regularity.

lateral_torso_inclination: G1 supports the torso's static gravity direction. Side-lying places gravity along the anatomical lateral direction, unlike supine lying, supplying an independent distinction without inventing movement differences. Standing, sitting and supine lying anchor low lateral inclination, but this split has no clear sustained high-level seen anchor, limiting learned zero-shot coverage. Anatomical sensor alignment is necessary; mounting rotation, partial rolling and dynamic acceleration are ambiguities.

leg_motion_alternation: G6 and G14 support recurring multiaxial leg-motion structure; the bilateral leg sensors can reveal alternating versus simultaneous movement timing. Walking and cycling provide alternating seen anchors, while jumping provides a largely synchronous anchor. This connects running and stepper to seen exercise and adds a rowing-versus-stepper distinction independent of posture variability. Short windows, asymmetry, pauses and unequal sensor alignment can obscure timing; absence of alternation does not distinguish stillness from synchronous movement without intensity.

semantic_redundancy_review: The 11 attributes describe distinct physical aspects. Intensity is magnitude, cadence is rate, regularity is predictability, and alternation is bilateral coordination. Smoothness concerns sustained fluctuations whereas impulsiveness concerns brief peaks. Mean global inclination, lateral torso inclination and posture variability describe configuration magnitude, directional orientation and temporal change, respectively. Rotational prominence is not equivalent to posture change, and translation is retained with explicit inertial-observability limits. No equipment identity, elevator-context indicator or assumed handle-use attribute is added. The additions do not guarantee separation of every pair or improve every coverage diagnostic; class-level assignments require separate review.
